reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a rule that only constrains a counterparty-favourable right; nothing actionable is required.

The AUDIT rule caps vendor audit rights against us, so the complete absence of any audit/inspection/records-examination or system-access right running against Sparkling is at least as favourable as the preferred position; proposing audit machinery would create a right that does not exist.

Cited paragraphs (§ 3 use restrictions at p0029/p0035/p0039 and the § 20 general-matters heading at p0134) contain only substantive use limits with no verification, reporting or access mechanism, consistent with the stated absence.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a false signal here: frequency-limiting language cannot appear where there is no audit clause; the rationale also correctly distinguishes the near-hits (escrow examination right in our favour at p0114 and the one-time post-termination cessation certification at p0118) as not audit rights.
No unnecessary text was altered — redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs, satisfying the minimal-edit expectation.
